div.head: Zizinia Theatre.
div.p: An exhibition of occult art will be given tomorrow evening at the Zizinia Theatre by the magician Melides.

div.head: Double Execution.
div.p: On Monday next at 8 a.m. two natives will be hanged at Hadra Prison for having murdered Ibrahim Khalfat in a shed belonging to the Railway Administration near Kafr Dawar.

div.head: Duem Government Building.
div.p: The Mudirieh offices at Duem have been removed to the new building recently erected in the outskirts of the town. The old Mudi-rieh will be used as a Post and Telegraph office.

div.head: Union Artistique Francaise.
div.p: This popular Alexandrian Society will give a concert to-morrow evening at its rooms at 4 Rosetta-street. The programme is excellent. On the following Saturday "Le Gendre de Monsieur Poirier" will be given.

div.head: The New Egyptian Company.
div.p: This Company will declare an interim divi- dend of ten per cent. This is very gratifying news and there is no doubt that it will have a most beneficial effect on the shares, which have been falling for some time.

div.head: Lord Cromer at Port Sald.
div.p: A slight error occurred in our correspon- dent's account of the reception of Lord and Lady Cromer by the residents of Port Said. The bouquet was presented to Lady Cromer by Mrs. Curling Hayward, not by Mrs. Snow as reported.

div.head: Discovery Near Helouan.
div.p: It is announced that a new sulphur spring has been discovered in the neighbourhood of Helouan. The water burst forth with such violence that it swept away two houses. Samples of the water are to be submitted to chemical analysis.

div.head: Brindisi Mall.
div.p: The following are the times at which the mail for Europe, via Port Said and Brindisi, will be made up :- Sunday: ordinary corres pondence 3.10 p.m., registered correspondence 2.10 p.m., insured articles and money orders at noon. Saturday: parcels 15 p.m.

div.head: Khartoums New Hospital.
div.p: The New Civil Hospital, will be built on a large plot of land situated at the Southern end of the city on Victoria Avenue A wall is being built now around the plot, and the build- ing itself will be commenced before long. The site is considered very suitable for the purpose. New Victoria Hotel.

div.head: From to-morrow an ofchestra of seven play- ers will perform on the spacious new terrace of the New Victoria Hotel at Ramleh daily from 5 to 10 p.m. under the bâton of Mr Jean d'Ambra. The popularity of this hotel is now well established, and we look forward to seeing its terrace, which can accommodate some 400 persons, erowded nightly.
The 8.8. Adelfotes.
div.p: The salvage steamer Warren Hastings which has succeeded in refloating the Greek SS. Adelfotes which went ashore near Agame, left" Alexandria to-day for Caiffa in order to save the Greek S.S. Cefalonia, which has stranded at Caiffa. The S.S. Adelfotes will be docked at Alexandria for repairs before she proceeds to Marseilles. The vessel was insured for £17,000 and is said to be damaged to the extent of £6,000.

div.head: "Realism in an Egyptian Play.
div.p: A feature in the staging of The Judgment of Pharaoh" at the Scala Theatre which pro- duced much banter in the home press was the introduction of a couple of Irish boar- hounds, made up as lions, which were intended to give an appearance of realism to the scene scene in which the hero is cast into the haunt of the beasts. Last week however, Dr. Distin Middick, the proprietor of the scala, conceived the idea of replacing these with real lions, but he received an intimation from the Lord Chamberlain that no exhibition of wild animals was allowed on the stage. In place of these, the management promise some- thing "sensational" in the future.
